newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine to shut one Chernobyl reactor next month.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine to shut one Chernobyl reactor next month.

text.p: Ukraine vowed on Monday to shut down one of two reactors still producing electricity at the Chernobyl nuclear plant on November 30, falling in line with a timetable agreed with Western donors.
"On November 30 Reactor Number One will be stopped completely," Environment and Nuclear Safety Minister Yuri Kostenko told a news conference.

Ukrainian officials had promised to shut down the reactor in November, but Kostenko said two weeks ago that stopping it as planned could make the station, scene of the world's worst nuclear accident, more prone to problems.

The fourth reactor at the plant exploded in 1986, sending a radioactive cloud across much of Europe. It is now encased in a cracking concrete "sarcophagus", while a second reactor was closed after a fire in 1991.
The two remaining reactors currently supply some five percent of Ukraine's electricity and Kostenko gave no indication of how this would be compensated for in the short term.

He said President Leonid Kuchma and his policy-making body, the Security Council, had agreed at the weekend that the shut-down should go ahead as planned. "All participants agreed that the reactor should be stopped on the 30th," Kostenko said.
Kiev has agreed to close the plant by 2000 in return for $3 billion in grants and funding from the Group of Seven leading industrialised nations.

The European Bank for Reconstruction and Development is expected to grant money to build two reactors at the Kmelnytsky and Rivne stations in western Ukraine to replace electricity lost by Chernobyl's closure.

Kostenko said the United States would give $27 million by next September to help make the sarcophagus safer. "Our main task is to create a long-term funding mechanism to shut the Chernobyl station and put an end to the problem," he said.
